headline: Record revenue cannot overcome the industry's heaviest debt load; American guides to a full-year loss as fuel costs jump 67%.
business: World's largest airline by fleet and passengers, with fortress hubs at Dallas/Fort Worth and Charlotte and a strong Latin America network. AAdvantage is a major profit pool, but the balance sheet still carries pandemic-era debt.
recent: Q3 2026 GAAP net loss of $269M ($0.41/share) and adjusted loss of $182M, despite record revenue of $16.3B (+19.3%).
Fuel costs rose $1.9B (+67.5%) as the price per gallon climbed to $3.85 from $2.37.
Full-year 2026 guided to an adjusted loss of $1.00-$1.60 per share; Q4 fuel assumed at about $4.70/gal; liquidity of $11.8B.
strengths: Dominant DFW and CLT hubs plus a valuable loyalty program
risks: $37B of debt: net debt/EBITDA of 8.4x, with negative book equity
Weakest operating margin of the big three (1.7%)
Lagging premium product vs. Delta and United
catalysts: Fuel price moves (very high operating leverage)
